# BoxyTrucks

> An enthusiast guide to boxy, body-on-frame 4x4s for hands-on owners: history, buying checks, DIY repairs with parts, service baselines, wheel and tire fitment, recalls, values and mods, one guide per generation. Facts are sourced on each page.

Fluid specs, capacities and torque figures are general guidance: always verify against the factory manual for the exact vehicle (see https://boxytrucks.com/about/disclaimer/). Parts links may be affiliate links.

Full text of every model guide: https://boxytrucks.com/llms-full.txt

## Toyota 4Runner

- [Toyota 4Runner overview](https://boxytrucks.com/models/4runner/): Toyota's mid-size body-on-frame survivor — forty years of refusing to become a crossover while everything around it did.
- [Toyota 4Runner 1st Gen (1984–1989)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/4runner/1st-gen/): A Hilux pickup with a removable fibreglass lid — solid front axle until the 1986 switch to independent front suspension.
- [Toyota 4Runner 2nd Gen (1990–1995)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/4runner/2nd-gen/): Still Hilux underneath, but with a one-piece steel body and a coil-sprung four-link rear axle.
- [Toyota 4Runner 3rd Gen (1996–2002)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/4runner/3rd-gen/): The one that left the pickup behind: Prado-shared chassis, coils all round, optional rear E-locker — the cult classic.
- [Toyota 4Runner 4th Gen (2003–2009)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/4runner/4th-gen/): Prado 120-based and bigger, with the only V8 4Runner (the 2UZ-FE) and X-REAS suspension on some trims.
- [Toyota 4Runner 5th Gen (2010–2024)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/4runner/5th-gen/): Fifteen model years on the J150 Prado/GX/FJ Cruiser platform with the 4.0 V6 — TRD Pro from 2015.
- [Toyota 4Runner 6th Gen (2025–present)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/4runner/6th-gen/): Moves to the TNGA-F (GA-F) frame shared with the Tacoma; turbo 2.4 four or the i-FORCE MAX hybrid, eight-speed auto.

## Ford Bronco

- [Ford Bronco overview](https://boxytrucks.com/models/bronco/): Ford's first SUV started as a 92-inch tin box with flat glass and a Dana 20, grew into an F-Series with a lift-off roof, vanished for 25 years and came back to fight the Jeep again. The first one is still the one everybody wants.
- [Ford Bronco (1966–1977) (1966–1977)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/bronco/early-bronco/): The original: a 92-inch-wheelbase roadster, half-cab or wagon with coil-sprung Dana 30/44 front, Ford 9-inch rear, Dana 20 and a six or a 289/302 V8.
- [Ford Full-size Bronco (1978–1996)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/bronco/full-size/): A short-wheelbase F-Series with a lift-off rear top: solid Dana 44 front axle and 351M/400 V8s in 1978–79, then Twin Traction Beam with the 300 six, 302 and 351W through 1996.
- [Ford Bronco (sixth generation) (2021–present)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/bronco/sixth-gen/): The revival on Ford's T6 frame: independent front suspension, solid rear axle, 2.3 and 2.7 EcoBoost, a seven-speed manual, the 35-inch Sasquatch package and the 37-inch Bronco Raptor.

## Mercedes-Benz G-Class

- [Mercedes-Benz G-Class overview](https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/): A military box that became the world’s most expensive school-run accessory. Still devastating off-road — which most owners will never find out.
- [Mercedes-Benz G-Class W460 (1979–1991)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/w460/): The original military-derived G, in short and long wheelbase, petrol and diesel.
- [Mercedes-Benz G-Class W461 (1992–2022)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/w461/): The no-frills working G for militaries and professionals, kept alongside the luxury W463.
- [Mercedes-Benz G-Class W463 (1990–2018)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/w463/): The civilian G: full-time 4WD, three lockers, ever-more luxury — and still solid axles.
- [Mercedes-Benz 500 GE V8 (1993–1994)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/500ge/): The limited-run first V8 G: 446 built, almost all in Amethyst Blue, with no front locker.
- [Mercedes-Benz Europa International Gs (1990s–2001)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/europa/): Federalized, US-VIN trucks imported by Europa of Santa Fe before Mercedes sold the G in America.
- [Mercedes-Benz G 500 (1998–2008)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/g500/): The first regular-production V8 G and the first sold by Mercedes in the US.
- [Mercedes-Benz G 55 AMG (1999–2012)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/g55-amg/): The hand-built AMG V8 version — the G that taught the world Gs could be fast.
- [Mercedes-Benz G 550 (2009–2018 (US))](https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/g550/): The G 500 renamed for the US, with a 5.5-litre V8 and seven-speed automatic.
- [Mercedes-Benz G 63 AMG (2012–2018 (US 2013–2018))](https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/g63-amg/): The biturbo AMG W463: 544–571 PS, seven speeds, and still three lockers on solid axles.
- [Mercedes-Benz G 63 AMG 6×6 (2013–2015)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/g63-6x6/): An Australian Army six-wheeler with the AMG V8, five lockers and tyre inflation from the cab; about 100 built.
- [Mercedes-Benz G 500 4×4² (2015–2018)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/4x4-squared/): Portal axles, enormous ground clearance and absolutely no subtlety.
- [Mercedes-Benz G-Class (second generation) (2018–present)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/g-class/second-gen/): Independent front suspension, a modern cabin and still three locking differentials.

## Ineos Grenadier

- [Ineos Grenadier overview](https://boxytrucks.com/models/grenadier/): A billionaire couldn't buy the old Defender, so he built his own from a pub table, a BMW engine and a pair of tractor axles. It is gloriously square, genuinely capable and steers like a canal boat (until 2026).
- [Ineos Grenadier Station Wagon (2022–present (US: 2024–present))](https://boxytrucks.com/models/grenadier/station-wagon/): The five-door, five-seat original: ladder frame, Carraro beam axles, BMW six, three lockable diffs available. US gets the petrol B58 only.
- [Ineos Grenadier Quartermaster (2023–present (US: 2025–present))](https://boxytrucks.com/models/grenadier/quartermaster/): Double-cab pickup on a 305 mm longer wheelbase, with a Euro-pallet-sized bed and up to 760 kg payload.

## International Scout

- [International Scout overview](https://boxytrucks.com/models/scout/): A tractor company's answer to the Jeep that accidentally invented the American SUV. Rusts like it's paid to, and owners forgive it every single time.
- [International Scout 80 / 800 (1961–1971)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/scout/scout-80-800/): The original Jeep fighter: four-cylinder Scout 80, then the more civilized 800 series with sixes and V8s.
- [International Scout II (1971–1980)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/scout/scout-ii/): The definitive Scout: IH V8s, Dana 44s, the 118-inch Traveler and Terra, a Nissan diesel and the Baja-winning SSII.
- [International Scout Motors Traveler & Terra (Announced 2022 · revealed 2024)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/scout/scout-motors/): Volkswagen Group's revival of the name, with a Traveler SUV and Terra pickup revealed in October 2024.

## Jeep

- [Jeep overview](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/): The Jeep is the boxy 4x4 everyone else gets compared to, even the ones that got there first. It leaks, rattles and rusts, and it keeps selling, mostly to people who have already owned three.
- [Jeep CJ-5 (1955–1983)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/cj-5/): Derived from the M38A1 military Jeep. Rounded door cutouts, Kaiser then AMC power, and 603,303 built across 29 years.
- [Jeep CJ-7 (1976–1986)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/cj-7/): The CJ-5's 10-inch-longer, square-door evolution: room for an automatic, optional hardtop and steel doors, and AMC's 258 six. Nearly 380,000 were built.
- [Jeep CJ-8 Scrambler (1981–1986)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/cj-8/): A CJ-7 stretched to a 103.5-inch wheelbase, with a removable half cab and a small pickup bed. Ronald Reagan kept one at his ranch.
- [Jeep Grand Wagoneer (SJ) (1984–1991)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/grand-wagoneer/): The full-size SJ wagon that began as the 1963 Wagoneer, renamed Grand Wagoneer for its final luxury-V8 years.
- [Jeep Cherokee XJ (1984–2001)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/cherokee-xj/): The compact unibody Cherokee, with the 4.0-liter straight six from 1987. It was the template for the modern SUV.
- [Jeep Comanche MJ (1986–1992)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/comanche-mj/): The Cherokee XJ turned into a compact pickup: XJ unibody up front, a fully boxed frame behind the cab, two bed lengths and the 4.0 six from 1987. 190,446 were built.
- [Jeep Wrangler YJ (1987–1995)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/yj/): The first Wrangler, with square headlights and leaf springs. Track bars and anti-roll bars made it more civil than the CJ.
- [Jeep Wrangler TJ (1997–2006)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/tj/): Coil springs and round headlights return on the short wheelbase. Many people think it's the best-riding classic Wrangler.
- [Jeep Wrangler Unlimited (LJ) (2004–2006)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/tj-unlimited/): The long-wheelbase TJ: more cargo room, a calmer ride and a short production run.
- [Jeep Wrangler JK (2-door) (2007–2018)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/jk/): A bigger, wider and more refined two-door Wrangler. In the US it had V6 power: a 3.8 at first, then the 3.6-liter Pentastar from 2012.
- [Jeep Wrangler JK Unlimited (2007–2018)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/jk-unlimited/): The first four-door Wrangler, and the one that took Jeep from niche toy to family car.
- [Jeep Wrangler JL (2018–present)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/jl/): The current two-door Wrangler, more modern inside and out, refreshed for 2024.
- [Jeep Wrangler JL Unlimited (2018–present)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/jl-unlimited/): The four-door JL, including the 4xe plug-in hybrid and the V8 Rubicon 392.
- [Jeep Gladiator JT (2020–present)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/jeep/gladiator-jt/): A JL Unlimited with a 137.3-inch wheelbase and a five-foot bed: Jeep's first pickup since the Comanche, with a 3.6 V6 or, for 2021–23, the 3.0 EcoDiesel. Refreshed for 2024.

## Toyota Land Cruiser

- [Toyota Land Cruiser overview](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-cruiser/): The truck the rest of the world actually depends on — the one that turns up, fully loaded, in places where a breakdown isn't an inconvenience but a plot twist. Seven decades in, Toyota still hasn't figured out how to make it fragile.
- [Toyota Land Cruiser FJ40 (1960–1984)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-cruiser/fj40/): The two-door, short-wheelbase icon on leaf springs and F/2F straight-sixes — the truck that made the Land Cruiser name in America.
- [Toyota Land Cruiser FJ45 / FJ55 (1960–1984 (FJ45) · 1967–1980 (FJ55))](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-cruiser/fj45-fj55/): The long-wheelbase 40 Series pickups and wagons, and the FJ55 'Iron Pig' — Toyota's first Land Cruiser designed from the start as a wagon.
- [Toyota Land Cruiser FJ60 (1980–1987)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-cruiser/fj60/): The square-rigged 60 Series wagon in its original form: carbureted 2F six, manual gearboxes, round headlights and leaf springs all round.
- [Toyota Land Cruiser FJ62 (1988–1990)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-cruiser/fj62/): The 60 grows up: fuel-injected 3F-E, automatic gearbox, square headlights and the first push upmarket.
- [Toyota Land Cruiser 70 Series (1984–present)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-cruiser/70-series/): The heavy-duty workhorse — wagons, troop carriers and pickups — still built for Africa, Australia, Latin America and the Middle East, and back on sale in Japan since 2023.
- [Toyota Land Cruiser 80 Series (1990–1997)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-cruiser/80-series/): Coil springs, full-time 4WD, solid axles at both ends and optional triple lockers — for many owners, the last 'real' Land Cruiser.
- [Toyota Land Cruiser 100 Series (1998–2007)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-cruiser/100-series/): The big wagon goes upmarket: V8 power (and, for the US, independent front suspension) and the basis for the Lexus LX 470.
- [Toyota Land Cruiser 200 Series (2007–2021)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-cruiser/200-series/): The V8 flagship and the last full-size Land Cruiser wagon sold in North America before Toyota pulled it after 2021.
- [Toyota FJ Cruiser (2007–2014 (US) · to 2022 elsewhere)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-cruiser/fj-cruiser/): The retro FJ40 tribute on a Prado-family frame: 4.0 V6, a six-speed manual with full-time 4WD or an automatic with part-time 4WD, and a factory rear locker. Sold in the US for 2007–2014 and built for other markets until 2022.
- [Toyota Land Cruiser 250 Series (2024–present (US))](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-cruiser/250-series/): The Prado-based 'light-duty' Land Cruiser that brought the name back to the US: TNGA-F platform, 326-hp i-FORCE MAX hybrid, full-time 4WD with center and rear lockers standard.
- [Toyota Land Cruiser 300 Series (2021–present)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-cruiser/300-series/): The current global flagship, unveiled in June 2021 — and not sold in the US or Canada.

## Land Rover Series & Defender

- [Land Rover Series & Defender overview](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-rover/): The original farm-gate-to-Sahara tool: slow, leaky, drafty, and still the shape every other boxy 4x4 gets measured against.
- [Land Rover Series I–III (1948–1985)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-rover/series/): Leaf springs, aluminium panels, selectable 4WD: the agricultural original that put the world's backcountry on wheels.
- [Land Rover 90 / 110 / Defender (1983–2016)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-rover/defender-90-110/): Coil springs and permanent 4WD from the Range Rover under a Series-shaped body; named Defender from 1990, built until January 2016.
- [Land Rover Defender (L663) (2020–present)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-rover/defender-l663/): The reboot: aluminium monocoque and independent suspension, unveiled September 2019 and launched as a 2020 model, officially sold in the US again.
- [Land Rover Discovery Series I (1989–1998)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-rover/discovery-1/): Range Rover Classic chassis, suspension and 4WD under a cheaper family body; sold in the US from the 1994 model year.
- [Land Rover Discovery Series II (1998–2004)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-rover/discovery-2/): The last Discovery on a ladder frame with live axles: Discovery 1 bones, P38 V8 and running gear, and a stack of electronics (ACE, SLS, HDC). Sold in the US for 1999–2004 as V8 automatics only.
- [Land Rover LR3 / Discovery 3 (2004–2009 (US: 2005–2009))](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-rover/lr3/): Ford-era clean sheet: Integrated Body Frame, four-corner air suspension and Terrain Response; V8 or V6 petrol as the LR3 in North America, TDV6 diesel elsewhere.
- [Land Rover LR4 / Discovery 4 (2009–2016 (US: 2010–2016))](https://boxytrucks.com/models/land-rover/lr4/): Discovery 3 reworked with new engines and cabin: the last Discovery with a separate frame, cross-linked air suspension and Terrain Response; sold as the LR4 in North America.

## Lexus LX & GX

- [Lexus LX & GX overview](https://boxytrucks.com/models/lexus/): Land Cruisers that went to finishing school and somehow kept their boots on. The badge says country club; the frame rails say Gobi Desert.
- [Lexus LX 450 (1996–1997)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/lexus/lx450/): The first Lexus truck, a lightly disguised 80 Series Land Cruiser with a 212-hp 4.5-liter straight-six. Sold for two US model years only.
- [Lexus LX 470 (1998–2007)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/lexus/lx470/): 100 Series Land Cruiser underneath, with the 4.7-liter 2UZ-FE V8 and hydraulic Adjustable Height Control (AHC) suspension.
- [Lexus LX 570 (2008–2021)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/lexus/lx570/): The 200 Series twin, powered by the 5.7-liter 3UR-FE V8 (383 hp in US/Canada trim).
- [Lexus LX 600 (2022–present)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/lexus/lx600/): Unveiled in October 2021 on the 300 Series platform. Swaps the V8 for a 409-hp 3.4-liter twin-turbo V6.
- [Lexus GX 470 (2003–2009)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/lexus/gx470/): Prado 120 underneath, with the 2UZ-FE V8 and a full-time 4WD system that has a locking center diff. Today it's one of the best-value overland platforms money can buy.
- [Lexus GX 460 (2010–2023)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/lexus/gx460/): Prado 150-based, with a 301-hp 4.6-liter V8, six-speed automatic and Torsen center locking differential. It famously earned (and lost) a Consumer Reports 'Don't Buy' in 2010.
- [Lexus GX 550 (2024–present)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/lexus/gx550/): Boxy again, and proud of it. It shares the GA-F platform with the Land Cruiser 250 and uses a 349-hp 3.4-liter twin-turbo V6.

## Nissan Patrol

- [Nissan Patrol overview](https://boxytrucks.com/models/nissan-patrol/): The Land Cruiser's oldest sparring partner, and the one Americans mostly know from imported photos of the Outback. The coil-sprung GQ and GU are the reason Australians still argue about which Japanese wagon is tougher.
- [Nissan Patrol Y60 (GQ) (1987–1997)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/nissan-patrol/y60/): The first coil-sprung Patrol: solid axles at both ends, TB42, TD42 and RD28T sixes, and a Ford Maverick twin in Australia.
- [Nissan Patrol Y61 (GU) (1997–2016 (later in some markets))](https://boxytrucks.com/models/nissan-patrol/y61/): The GQ's heavier, wider successor on the same solid-axle layout: TB48 and TD42T heroes, the ZD30's troubles, and utes and cab-chassis that outlived the wagon.

## Land Rover Range Rover

- [Land Rover Range Rover overview](https://boxytrucks.com/models/range-rover/): The truck that taught a farm tool to wear a suit — and, for its first quarter-century, never forgot where it parked its wellies.
- [Land Rover Range Rover Classic (1970–1996)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/range-rover/classic/): The original: two-door then four-door, coil springs, Rover V8, and a 24-year run that created the luxury 4x4.
- [Land Rover Range Rover P38A (1994–2002)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/range-rover/p38/): Last of the ladder-frame, live-axle Range Rovers — 4.0/4.6 Rover V8s, standard air suspension and a lot more electronics.
- [Land Rover Range Rover L322 (2002–2012)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/range-rover/l322/): Monocoque body and all-independent air suspension; BMW-era engines at launch, Ford-era engines from 2005.
- [Land Rover Range Rover L405 (2012–2021)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/range-rover/l405/): All-aluminium monocoque that shed more than 400 kg versus the steel L322.
- [Land Rover Range Rover L460 (2022–present)](https://boxytrucks.com/models/range-rover/l460/): Fifth generation, revealed October 2021: seven-seat option, plug-in hybrids and a BMW-sourced 4.4 V8.
